entries.comment: Creatures: Fauna of Crateria and Brinstar
entries.content:
Crateria is the storm-lashed surface of Zebes, pelted by meteors and acid rain; Brinstar is the humid cavern jungle beneath it, thick with carnivorous plants and home to more than sixty percent of the planet's life. Samus Aran grew up on Zebes among the Chozo. Per the manga, when Kreatz spotted a Skree hanging overhead she warned that the planet "has predators found nowhere else in the galaxy"; it then ripped through a Space Pirate travelling with them. She fought through both regions on her first Zebes mission (Metroid: Zero Mission) and again while hunting the stolen baby Metroid (Super Metroid).
- Zoomer and Geemer: small spiked crawlers that circle floors, walls and ceilings on fixed paths; per the manual they excrete a sticky liquid from their feet. Yellow Zoomers are the feeblest; red ones and the larger Geemer are far tougher. "Zoomer" began as a mistranslation of the Japanese name later rendered Geemer.
- Ripper: armor-shelled fliers (brainless, per the manual) drifting in straight lines. Beams and missiles bounce off; the Screw Attack or Speed Booster destroys one, and the Ice Beam freezes them into footholds. The jet-propelled Ripper II is faster.
- Skree: bat-like ambushers that hang from ceilings, drop on anything passing beneath, bore into the ground and burst into shrapnel. The armored Metaree is a tougher relative.
- Reo: clawed, fly-like divers swooping from the upper walls; per the manual, red ones outclass yellow.
- Waver: fliers whose two armored flaps close into a shield; they flutter and ram.
- Sidehopper: thick-legged pouncers that can even hop along ceilings. Three oversized ones in Tourian could be hurt only by Super Missiles, and the baby Metroid killed the last before Samus could.
- Zeb, Zebbo and Geega: insects that pour one after another from Brinstar's pipes and air holes to dive at intruders.
- Beetom: leapers that latch on and cling like miniature Metroids; bombs and missiles harm them, beams do not.
- Cacatac: walking cactus-plants firing thorn volleys.
- Zeela: eyestalked crawlers on fixed paths.
- Kago: insect nests that erupt in swarms only if disturbed.
- Fireflea: bioluminescent drifters, the only light in Brinstar's darkest rooms.
- Samus Eater and Yapping Maw: a flower whose petals clamp shut on prey, and a buried pincer-worm that lunges out to seize passers-by.
See also: Kraid, Spore Spawn, the Torizo, the Etecoons, the Dachora, Zebesians and Kihunters.
entries.notes: Kept the Zoomer 'sticky liquid' manual line: the fact-check called it unverified, but Metroid Wiki's Zoomer page quotes both the Metroid and Zero Mission manuals saying so. Dropped bare keys Zoomer-risk accepted (in-universe usage dominates in a Samus RP); Ripper, Rippers, Waver, Wavers, Zeb, Zebs dropped as generic English or common names (still described in content). Tripper not keyed (generic English). Manga Skree scene reframed per Metroid Wiki (Kreatz spots it; it then kills a Zebesian). Added Tourian Sidehopper/baby Metroid beat and the Zoomer/Geemer naming note. Skultera/Sciser/Alcoon closing sentence moved out (covered by Norfair and Maridia entries).

entries.content:
Norfair is the volcanic underworld of Zebes: lakes of magma, superheated caverns and boiling streams of acid, with Ridley's lair in its depths and, by Samus Aran's second visit, a massive Space Pirate base. Samus crossed Norfair on both of her Zebes missions. On the second (Super Metroid) she found it heavily flooded with lava since her first visit and survivable only in the Varia Suit, and in Ridley's lair she found the baby Metroid's broken capsule.
- Nova (also recorded as Sova): crawlers covered, per the manual, in "spiky, fireproof wool," creeping along floors and ceilings, dripping flaming fluid; blue ones are weaker than yellow. Some were later taken to the BSL station and the Bottle Ship.
- Gamet: hard-shelled fliers that burst from air holes or magma in vertical stacks to dive at a target; per the manual, red Gamets have twice the strength of the others.
- Geruta: armored, hot-blooded fliers with huge forearms that swoop in wave-like glides to rake prey; red ones are the stronger kind.
- Multiviola and Viola: fiery orange orbs that careen through caverns rebounding off walls, and their blue larval form, bound to patches of rock.
- Holtz: armored hoverers of lower Norfair and Ridley's lair that hang still, then swoop on jets of ignited bio-propellant, even through lava.
- Squeept: crustacean-like leapers that spring from magma pools to grab prey; freezable into stepping stones.
- Dragon and Alcoon: seahorse-shaped fire-spitters that rise from lava and sink back, and a bipedal relative that leaps from beneath the ground spitting three fireballs (red in Norfair, green in Crateria).
- Magdollite: hulking lava-coated humanoids that lurk with only their faces above the surface, then fling globs of lava; only Super Missiles or Power Bombs kill them.
- Fune and Namihe: serpents living inside rock walls with only their heads showing (the Fune eyeless, hunting by hearing), spitting globules that burst into flame. A Fune can be destroyed or frozen; a Namihe can only be frozen briefly.
- Mella and Memu: tiny swarming fliers; the fiercer Memu infest Ridley's hideout and pass through walls.
- Puromi: indestructible fiery serpents of an acid pool.
- Dessgeega: larger, spine-studded relatives of the Sidehopper, aggressive on sight.
Zebbos rise from Norfair's acid, and Cacatacs, Kagos and Yapping Maws persist here. See also: Ridley, Crocomire, the Golden Torizo.
entries.notes: Nova/Sova: Metroid Wiki redirects Sova to Nova; Metroid Database treats Sova as correct. Bare 'Nova'/'Novas' and 'Holtz' dropped from keys (common word / surname); 'Sova' keeps the creature reachable. Geruta colours softened to 'red ones are the stronger kind' (Metroid Database lists red and pink, never purple). Gamet colour detail labelled 'per the manual'. Fune-only eyelessness per Metroid Database. Added the lava-flooding and broken-capsule facts (Metroid Wiki Norfair and Super Metroid pages). Tripper sentence removed. 'Dragon' and 'Viola' not keyed (generic English).

entries.comment: Creatures: Fauna of Maridia and the Wrecked Ship
entries.content:
Maridia is the flooded quarter of Zebes bordering Brinstar and Crateria: underwater tunnels, sandy caverns and quicksand, home to Draygon, Botwoon and a submerged Space Pirate research facility. Samus Aran entered it by breaking open a tunnel in the middle of Brinstar with a Power Bomb, could not move freely in its water until she took the Gravity Suit from the Wrecked Ship, and came away with the Space Jump, Plasma Beam and Spring Ball while hunting the stolen baby Metroid (Super Metroid). The Wrecked Ship is a crashed vessel on Crateria's surface, left powerless by Phantoon.
Maridia:
- Mochtroid: per the manual, "the Space Pirates' first attempt at Metroid clones"; frail things that drain energy but cannot latch on. They were Samus's first evidence that the Pirates were cloning Metroids.
- Evir: hard-shelled drifters that ride the sand currents, firing projectiles even while buried; a swarm attended Draygon and carried its corpse away.
- Owtch: spike-shelled crawlers that burrow into sand when they sense danger.
- Puyo: small green blobs that hop at intruders in short arcs.
- Powamp: placid gas-sacs that inflate when threatened and serve as anchors for the Grapple Beam.
- Zoa: shrimp-like hoverers that rise from the sand one after another in groups.
- Yard: clawed snails that climb any surface and withdraw into armored shells; only explosives harm them.
- Tatori: a turtle-like giant easily mistaken for a mossy rock, violently protective of its young.
- Oum: nautilus-like rollers with indestructible shells; only three were ever seen.
- Bull: hollow, gas-filled spore sacs that vent gas to ram intruders; they also drift through the Wrecked Ship.
- Choot: flat amphibians that leap straight up and glide down onto passers-by.
- Sciser and Skultera: red armored crustaceans that climb the underwater walls, and bony armored fish on fixed patrol routes.
Wrecked Ship:
- Covern (Koben): skull-clusters the manual calls "souls of shipwrecked creatures" that "wrap themselves around intruders"; they materialize while the power is out and vanish once it returns.
- Atomic: beings of pure energy sealed in glass chambers until the power returns, then drifting free to shock anything they touch.
- Work Robot: slow, cylindrical bipedal machines, inert until the ship wakes, then firing ring-beams at anything that moves; indestructible.
Kago nests, Cacatacs, Yapping Maws and Boyons round out the two regions. See also: Phantoon, Draygon, Botwoon.
entries.notes: Removed 'ancient flood' and 'beneath Brinstar' (Metroid Wiki: borders Brinstar and Crateria, entered via a Power Bombed tunnel in mid-Brinstar; flood origin uncited). Zoa softened to Metroid Database wording. 'Breeding' corrected to 'cloning'; Mochtroid manual quote replaced with the line Metroid Wiki actually cites. Added entry route and Maridia acquisitions. 'Bull', 'Yard', 'Atomic', 'Atomics' and 'Work Robot(s)' not keyed (generic English). Work Robot's Chozo origin asserted only by Metroid Database, so omitted.

entries.content:
SR388, the Metroid homeworld, is a maze of caverns, acid pools and abandoned Chozo ruins whose machines still patrol. The Chozo created the Metroids there to combat the X parasites, which had killed everything on the planet like a plague. Samus Aran crossed SR388 on her Metroid extermination mission (Metroid II / Samus Returns). Years later, escorting a Biologic Space Laboratories research team on the surface, she shot a Hornoad and was infected by the X that emerged from it; the planet was destroyed at the end of the BSL incident (Metroid Fusion).
- Hornoad: frog-like hoppers with clawed feet that attack intruders but quickly lose interest if they move away. Per the manga, Old Bird described it to his fellow Chozo as a "silly creature that hops around" that turns hostile once an X mimics it. After Samus's extermination mission, a Hornoad tried to eat one of Proteus Ridley's severed arms and an X emerged and took it over.
- Tsumuri, Needler and Moheek: snail-, urchin- and anemone-like crawlers on walls and ceilings, harmless unless touched.
- Moto: armored, fiercely territorial chargers, soft only at the rear.
- Gravitt and Ramulken: a crab that hides in sand disguised as spikes and scuttles off when disturbed, and an armored one-eyed crustacean vulnerable only at its underbelly.
- Yumbo, Mumbo, Septogg and Senjoo: weak patrolling fliers; the Yumbo bears a spinning spiked appendage before its face, the docile Septogg can briefly carry Samus, and the Senjoo rams with spiked rings.
- Gullugg: big-eyed, bat-winged circlers that strike hard.
- Yumee and Gawron: nest insects that erupt one after another.
- Drivel and Skreek: bat-like hunters of the deepest caverns that drop corrosive, explosive saliva, and lava-lurking ambushers that leap out spitting paralytic blobs.
- Halzyn: helium-shelled drifters, harmless until X infection taught them to snap shut and drop.
- Chute Leech and Octroll: flat, camouflaged leapers that spring up and glide down onto prey, and a cephalopod relative floating in acid pools.
- Blob Thrower: a huge rooted flower that spews spores.
- Glow Fly and Skorp: wall-clinging glowers that are the only natural light underground, and wall-burrowing arachnids with sawblade claws.
Chozo machines: Wallfire (bird-shaped wall sentries spitting fireballs), Autoad (hopping robots "out of control"), Autrack (laser guardians with extending necks), Autom (flamethrower units), Gunzoo (armored security drones) and Shirk (spiked circling drones). See also: Arachnus, the Diggernaut, Metroids, X Parasites.
entries.notes: Replaced the non-canon 'first creature taken over by an X' trivia with the manga line; Metroid Wiki attributes it to Old Bird addressing other Chozo (Vol. 1 Ch. 4), not the young Samus as the fact-check suggested. Removed all five Samus Returns-only behaviours (snippet-sourced). Fixed Yumbo appendage, Gravitt (scuttles, no stabbing) and Shirk (circling). Added the Chozo-created-Metroids context and the Proteus Ridley arm/Hornoad X scene. 'Moto', 'Needler', 'Mumbo' (mumbo jumbo), 'Glow Fly', 'Drivel' and 'Shirk' not keyed to avoid misfires; Autom keyed; Seerook source dropped (not covered).

entries.content:
ZDR is the Chozo-held world where Samus Aran was stranded after Raven Beak stripped her abilities, hunted by the rogue E.M.M.I. (Metroid Dread). Its wildlife is native and often ancient; its research sites are patrolled by robots believed to use advanced Chozo technology. Samus met most of it with her Arm Cannon and the Melee Counter. After the X escaped quarantine in Elun they overran the whole planet, and creatures everywhere became X hosts, releasing an X when killed.
Artaria (the cold, cavernous depths where Samus awoke):
- Klaida: four-legged, unarmored natives that never attack but hurt and repel anything touching them.
- Ply: small fliers with an eyeball-like head that charge with a spiked tail, sometimes in groups.
- Muzby: large, faceless two-legged brutes with heavy arms and tough hide. An X-infected, mutated Muzby became Golzuna.
Cataris (where the planet's energy-generating magma is circulated):
- Vulkran: small creatures that cling to any surface, store magma and spit several shots when threatened.
- Autclast: robots whose side cylinders slam down, sending fire along the ground.
- Obsydomithon: rock-like creatures dormant as ore near magma until roused, then firing a heat blast that passes through terrain.
Dairon (a biological research site, partly dark from power failures):
- Autsharp and Autsniper: robots that launch from docks behind a spinning energy blade, and small treaded robots that climb walls and ceilings to fire a precise laser.
- Armadigger: violent four-legged natives that charge, wheel and charge again.
Burenia (a marine research site, its lower half underwater):
- Batalloon: deceptively durable floaters that drift toward whoever hits them.
- Dizzean: small jellyfish, weak alone but gathering in large groups.
- Slaaga: creatures that store acid in a yellow hump and fire it with precision.
Ghavoran (a sunlit underground forest near the surface):
- Hecathon: large creatures present on ZDR since ancient times; they usually ignore Samus but unleash a disintegrating light when struck.
- Yampa: spider-like stalkers that lunge with a strong bite but cannot reach a ledge above or below their own.
- Quetzoa: mid-sized insect-like fliers that home in and charge at high speed. A mutated Quetzoa became Escue.
Ferenia and Hanubia: Sabotoru, slug-like crawlers that rush to the nearest door and block it by spreading their bodies and extending spikes.
See also: Chozo Soldiers, Robot Chozo Soldiers, E.M.M.I., Corpius, Drogyga, Escue, Golzuna, Experiment Z-57, Mawkin.
entries.notes: Fifteen creatures and the area descriptions follow Nintendo's official Metroid Dread Report Vol. 8. Golzuna (X-mutated Muzby) and Escue (mutated Quetzoa) per Metroid Wiki's ZDR page. Sabotoru kept after a search snippet (quoting Wikitroid) confirmed its Ferenia/Hanubia placement and door-blocking behaviour. Dropter, Caterzilla, Daivo, Slidle and Blindfly removed: one further search found no source. 'Blindflyer' key dropped. Autclast hedged as 'thought to be of Chozo make' per Nintendo's wording. 'Ply' not keyed (generic English).

entries.comment: Creatures: Fauna of the Bottle Ship
entries.content:
The Bottle Ship was a Galactic Federation vessel built, against Federation protocol, to cultivate bioweapons: the jungle Sector 1 (Biosphere), the frigid Sector 2 (Cryosphere), the volcanic Sector 3 (Pyrosphere), the Main Sector and the Bioweapon Research Center. Many of its specimens were clones of Zebes species, so when Samus Aran investigated alongside Adam Malkovich's 07th Platoon (Metroid: Other M) she met creatures she had thought lost with that planet. A Gigafraug corpse in the Cryosphere bearing signs of Metroid predation warned her that Metroids were loose aboard.
Zebes clones:
- Reo, Geemer and Skree: Reos burst from biomass nests and grip Samus; cloned Skrees do not self-destruct and dive repeatedly. The Cyclaw, a seemingly mechanically enhanced Skree, exists only here.
- Zero: Kihunter larvae that leap at intruders and, left undisturbed, pupate into cocoons from which adult Kihunters emerge.
- Mella and Himella: flame-spitting swarmers and their ice-adapted kin, which fire ice shards in the Cryosphere.
- Waver, Sidehopper, Dessgeega, Nova, Magdollite, Skultera, Rinka, Fune and Namihe also thrive in its sectors.
Natives and designs:
- Ghalmanian: chameleon-like Biosphere creatures that turn invisible, then headbutt or spit acid.
- Griptian and Mighty Griptian: armadillo-like beasts that roll into a ball to ram, claw and burrow.
- Dragotix: large creatures, docile unless something enters their zone of perception.
- Groganch: six-legged, tree-like giants camouflaged by bark-like skin, firing gas-filled globes from an orange abdominal bulb.
- Kyratian: amphibian-like Cryosphere humanoids with electrical coils on their backs that hurl electric orbs.
- Fumbleye, Joulion, Volfon and Gigafraug, also of the Cryosphere: a one-eyed ceiling polyp that grabs victims and flings them into water; hovering water-flea creatures that shock and explode; horned beasts reported to hunt in packs of three; and a massive armored brute.
- Rhedogian: one-eyed flying behemoths that ram, fire Seeker Missiles and charge an eye laser that can kill outright. One ambushed Samus on a Cryosphere elevator after she cut down seven Super Zebesians, attacked Anthony Higgs above the Pyrosphere's lava until she rescued him, and died in the Biosphere, where she took its Seeker Missiles.
- Desbrachian: dormant ovoid creatures disguised as the alarms above doors; a Power Bomb wakes them, and MB woke them telepathically to annihilate Federation soldiers. They move at high speed, grab and slam.
- Brug: tiny swarmers that gather around an Emperor Brug into a single Brug Mass.
See also: Vorash, Goyagma, King Kihunter, Nightmare, the Ridley clone, the Queen Metroid, Phantoon, MB.
entries.notes: Desbrachian 'teleport' corrected to high-speed movement; disguise as door alarms and MB's telepathic awakening against Federation soldiers per Metroid Wiki's MB page. Little Birdie/Dragotix link removed. Mighty Griptian Screw Attack immunity removed (unverified). Groganch weak point corrected to an orange abdominal bulb and Himella to ice shards, per a search whose snippets quote Wikitroid; Volfon 'packs of three' rests on one player guide, hence 'reported'. Kyratian, Ghalmanian and Dragotix descriptions remain snippet-sourced (no Metroid Wiki pages). Added Gigafraug predation victim and Rhedogian elevator/Super Zebesian beat (Metroid Wiki Bottle Ship, Cryosphere and Rhedogian pages). 'Zero' not keyed (forbidden bare key).

entries.comment: Creatures: Fauna of the BSL station
entries.content:
The Biologic Space Laboratories research station (BSL) orbited SR388 and kept specimens from that planet, from Zebes and from farther afield in sealed habitats: Sector 1 (SRX, an SR388 analogue), Sector 2 (TRO, tropical), Sector 3 (PYR, volcanic), Sector 4 (AQA, aquatic), Sector 5 (ARC, arctic), Sector 6 (NOC, nocturnal) and the Main Deck. During the BSL incident (Metroid Fusion) the X parasites killed and mimicked nearly all of them, so the creatures Samus Aran met were X copies, often larger, more aggressive or newly armed, each releasing an X she could absorb through her Fusion Suit. Adam, her AI commanding officer, warned that the X were evolving and that some now resisted her weapons. Samus knew many of the originals from Zebes and SR388.
Main Deck and SRX:
- Hornoad: mimicked ones spit damaging fluid, while the few uninfected ones never attack.
- Zombie Researcher: station crew taken by the X, per the manual "probably the result of X parasite absorbing a slime creature's DNA"; shambling, weak, and regenerated whenever an X re-enters the body. Adam judged that the X infected the humans for knowledge and that the others were merely food.
- Moto: territorial armored chargers, soft only at the rear.
- Halzyn: helium-shelled drifters that snap shut and drop on whatever is beneath.
- Yameba: floating amoeba-like X masses that settle on prey and drain it, merging into larger blobs.
- Genesis: large crawlers in dark ceiling spaces, drooling caustic saliva.
- Geruboss and Geruda: X-enhanced Gerutas; the Geruboss has metallic claws and shrugs off beams, the Geruda glides upright.
TRO: Zero-X (also rendered Zoro), the Kihunter larvae, red and far tougher blue; Reo, Ripper, Dessgeega, spiked red Puyo, Skultera, and Kago nests swollen into damaging columns.
PYR: Sova leaving trails of flaming droppings, Sidehopper, Squeept, and Fune and Namihe striking from holes in the walls.
AQA: Skultera in large and golden varieties, Evir with orbiting projectiles, Owtch, nearly indestructible Powamp, Yard, and Sciser with thickened spiked shells and plasma-firing claws, clustering into Gold Scisers.
ARC: Ripper, Waver, Kago and the Chute, adapted by the X to the cold and armed with acidic vomit.
NOC: Memu, one-eyed swarmers, and Zozoro, large glowing cave worms clinging to ceilings.
Gelon: inert X masses blocking passages until cleared with missiles or Power Bombs.
See also: Zebesians, Kihunters, Blue X, Arachnus, Zazabi, Serris, Yakuza, Nettori, Nightmare, Neo-Ridley, SA-X, Adam Malkovich.
entries.notes: Metroid Wiki redirects Zoro to Zero and calls the mimics Zero-X; both forms keyed, bare 'Zoro'/'Zoros' dropped (One Piece collision). Memu wall-passing removed (original-game trait). Added Adam's 'evolving, resisting your weapons' remark and his knowledge/food assessment with the manual quote (Metroid Wiki Zombie Researcher page). 'Moto-X' (phone brand), 'Geron' (company) and 'Genesis'/'Mimic' not keyed. Gelon, Geruboss and Genesis are unofficial or fan-database romanizations; Metroid Wiki has no pages for them. Sector abbreviations not keyed.
